name: tau

phase_0.boundary_condition: The electroweak symmetry breaking scale (v ≈ 246 GeV) and the Higgs mechanism that generates the tau mass and fixes its Yukawa coupling, closing the system within the Standard Model gauge structure SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y.

⊢.justification: The unbroken SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y symmetric vacuum before the Higgs field acquires its VEV; no tau mass, no chiral splitting, no third-generation lepton mass eigenstate exists.

⊣.justification: The Higgs VEV ⟨φ⟩ = v/√2 provides the terminal anchor: it generates the tau mass m_τ = y_τ v/√2, fixes the tau Yukawa coupling y_τ, and defines the electroweak scale that contains all tau interactions.

≻.justification: Forward morphism creating on-shell tau leptons from initial state; the tau moves forward in proper time from production vertex toward decay.

≺.justification: Contravariant descent: the heavy tau decays into lighter particles, reversing the mass hierarchy; the W⁻* virtuality carries the process backward toward the electroweak scale.

⋈.chosen_element: sequential decay vertices (τ → ν_τ W⁻ → ν_τ + hadrons/leptons)
⋈.justification: Composition of weak charged-current vertices: the tau decay chain links production, W emission, and W decay into a single amplitude ordered by proper time.

⊙.chosen_element: tau quantum numbers (Q = -1, L_τ = +1, m_τ = 1777 MeV)
⊙.justification: Self-reference: the tau identifies itself through its invariant quantum numbers — charge, tau lepton number, mass — which are preserved across all interactions and decays.

∈.justification: The tau decays into multiple exclusive channels: hadronic (τ⁻ → ν_τ + π⁻, ρ⁻, a₁⁻, ...) and leptonic (τ⁻ → ν_τ + e⁻ν̄_e, μ⁻ν̄_μ); the FSPLIT opens the hadronic arm (T) and leptonic arm (F) simultaneously.

∋.justification: Rejoins all exclusive branching fractions into the total decay rate; hadronic and leptonic arms fuse to the measured lifetime τ_τ = 2.903×10⁻¹³ s, where conflicting chiral structures (V-A vs scalar) recombine to B.

⊤.justification: Affirmative arm: the Standard Model weak interaction couples only to left-handed fermions; the tau's left-handed component participates fully in the charged current, depositing T.

⊥.justification: Negative arm: right-handed tau has no charged current coupling; CKM-suppressed channels (|V_ud|² vs |V_us|²) deposit F for disfavored hadronic modes.

⊞.justification: Paradice: the interference between tree-level and penguin amplitudes in hadronic tau decays holds both T (SM amplitude) and F (CP-violating phase) simultaneously without resolution — the B state is the live CP asymmetry.

⊡.justification: Irreversible fixation: the detector records the tau decay products (tracks, calorimeter clusters) as permanent, append-only data; the measurement cannot be undone and freezes the quantum state.

split_outputs: hadronic arm: τ⁻ → ν_τ + hadrons (π⁻, ρ⁻, a₁⁻, ...) via W⁻* → qq̄'
leptonic arm: τ⁻ → ν_τ + ℓ⁻ + ν̄_ℓ (ℓ = e, μ) via W⁻* → ℓ⁻ν̄_ℓ
phase_2.fuse_element: total decay rate measurement (Γ_τ = Σ_i Γ_i)
phase_2.fuse_result: measured tau lifetime τ_τ = 1/Γ_τ with branching fractions summing to unity

phase_3.void_description: Pre-electroweak vacuum: no tau field excitation, SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y unbroken, y_τ = 0, m_τ = 0
phase_3.true_description: On-shell tau lepton produced with correct quantum numbers: Q = -1, L_τ = +1, left-handed chirality engaged in charged current, mass shell p² = m_τ² satisfied
phase_3.false_description: Virtual/off-shell tau propagation, wrong-chirality vertex (right-handed charged current = 0), CKM-suppressed hadronic channel (|V_us|² ≪ |V_ud|²), or unphysical polarization state
phase_3.both_description: Quantum interference between decay amplitudes: e.g., τ⁻ → K⁻π⁰ν_τ tree vs penguin diagrams holding CP-even and CP-odd phases simultaneously; the B state is the live CP asymmetry A_CP measured in the angular distribution

phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Coherent tau quantum state: pure momentum, helicity, flavor eigenstate; zero entanglement with decay products

phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the weak decay is unitary at amplitude level; entropy increase from branching is compensated by information gain in detector measurement, preserving total quantum information
